messages:
maria: quick heads-up — ran a 1h perf profile on the host ingress path, saw a new tail on 95th latency after yesterday's preparse change

alex: can you paste the top traces?

maria: gist of flame: heavy time in tokenize_writev() and grpc::Writev(), also more syscalls around socket flushes

sam: is this for short seq chat requests or long context runs?

maria: mostly short seq (<128 tokens). batch sizes unchanged but we now see fewer microbatches and more per-request syscall overhead

jing: sounds like bundling got weaker — did autobatcher affinity change when we swapped the kernel selector?

maria: possible. kernel selector PR bumped heuristic to prefer small-kernel for mixed shapes — that may be preventing hot-path coalescing

tina: @alex any recent changes to batching heuristics?

alex: I tweaked the timer threshold (autobatcher.max_wait_ms  -> 3ms from 1ms) to reduce 429s. Should have reduced microbatch churn, not increased it tho

maria: profiling snippet:
```
  host_parse  42%  tokenize_writev
  grpc_writev 28%  syscall:sendmsg
  kvcache_eviction 12%  copy_buffer
  user+sys  98% total
```

paul: kvcache_eviction in host path?? that should be infra side — can you show trace IDs?

maria: http://perf.example/reports/611777 — trace 0x9f3a - eviction spikes correlate with requests that hit short-lived prefixes after a resume

sam: if tokenization is writing many small writes we lose coalescing at the socket level — maybe writev usage changed. any code change to tokenizer output flush?

maria: tokenizer used to batch tokens into slab buffers and call a single writev per frame. the preparse change introduced an early flush when encountering certain control tokens (\u201cEOS_MARK\u201d)

alex: ok that explains writev churn. two fixes: 1) revert early flush, 2) change autobatcher to wait-to-coalesce if sequence arrival rate > X

jing: careful: waiting longer affects P50 for interactive users. maybe make it conditional: only coalesce when estimated per-req tokenization cost < threshold

tina: what about grpc http2 HEADERS overhead? do we see more small frames?

maria: yes — tcpdump shows more 1-2 frame bursts, HTTP2 WINDOW_UPDATE spikes, a lot of small DATA frames ~512B

paul: could be TLS record packing + writev fragmentation. Are we setting MSG_MORE?

maria: I looked — MSG_MORE used in some paths but not downstream after preparse refactor. patch included missing flag in parser sink

alex: adding MSG_MORE back is low risk. also pushing a kernel-selector tweak: prefer the microkernel when seq_len < 64 and expected batch>1, else default. that should improve coalescing on CPU side

sam: also check KV cache eviction pattern. if tokenizers are flushing more prefixes, more tiny entries get inserted then evicted, which knocks background GC and increases CPU smoke

maria: agree. metric: kv.put_rate doubled in the spike window, kv.hit_rate dropped 7%

tina: proposed action list:
- revert early-flush in preparse (maria)
- restore MSG_MORE in tokenizer sink (maria)
- autobatcher conditional coalesce patch (alex)
- add eviction watermark telemetry and per-prefix TTL (paul)

alex: I'll open PRs for autobatcher and kernel-selector change, link to traces

maria: posted a minimal repro + perf flame in the perf link. will try revert in a canary env WIP

devops-bot: deploy requested by maria to canary-cluster-2 queued (run id: dpl-611777) :rocket:

paul: if canary looks good, we should run a 2h soak with traffic shaped for short-chat workload (ramp 100->1000 qps)

maria: agreed. I'll coordinate with loadgen and post numbers here

alex: thanks all — nice triage. follow-ups in threads on the PRs. :thumbsup:
